money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Nepalese Rupee (NPR). Declare all amounts of cash over $US5,000 or equivalent on arrival and departure. You can change foreign currency for NPR at banks or foreign exchange counters at the airport and in major tourist hubs. You cannot exchange NPR outside Nepal. Credit cards are accepted at major hotels and commercial places. ATMs are not common in remote places. Carry enough cash to cover your needs.

laws.rule: In tourist areas, it's common to be offered to buy drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe. Even if you're found with small quantities, authorities can convict and jail you.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Commercial surrogacy has been illegal since 2015.
laws.heading: Surrogacy laws

laws.rule: Australian and Nepalese authorities are committed to combating child sex offences. Penalties are severe under both Australian and Nepalese law. You can be punished either in Nepal or at home under Australian law. Penalties for having sex with anyone younger than 16 years include long jail times. It's illegal to take photos or videos of: army barracks checkpoints military personnel. It's illegal to seek to convert people from their religion. Punishment can include jail. If authorities suspect you're trying to convert people, you will likely be deported and banned from re-entering Nepal for years. Same-sex relationships are legal and Nepali LGBTQIA+ people actively advocate for their rights. H
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: To drive, you need both: a valid Australian driver's licence an International Driving Permit (IDP) Get your IDP before you leave Australia. Your travel and vehicle insurance could be void if you drive without an IDP. If you stay for longer than six months, you need a Nepali driver's licence. The minimum driving age is 18 years.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress codes are relaxed in tourist areas of Kathmandu and Pokhara. Other parts of the country are more conservative. Dress modestly to avoid offending locals, especially at religious sites and in rural areas. If in doubt, seek local advice. Nepal Tourism Board: walk clockwise around stupas and temples, remove shoes where required, and use your right hand. Some Hindu temples (for example Pashupatinath's main temple) admit Hindus only.

layers.process: On the specific protected-area treks listed by the Nepal Tourism Board, arrange a licensed trekking guide and agency-issued Trekkers Information Management System (TIMS) card through a government-registered trekking agency. The list includes Everest Base Camp, Gokyo, Manaslu Circuit, Tsum Valley, Annapurna Circuit, Upper Mustang, Upper Dolpo and Kanchenjunga. Check the precise route with the agency before booking: this is not a claim that every walk in Nepal requires a guide.

layers.authority: Nepal Department of Immigration; Nepal Tourism Board
layers.process: A separate Department of Immigration trekking permit is needed for routes in designated restricted areas. Keep the permit with you, follow the area and route it specifies, and show it to immigration or police on request. A TIMS card does not replace the restricted-area permit. Confirm the route, documents and processing time with the department or registered trekking agency.

The TIMS page lists NPR 2,000 per person for non-SAARC nationals and NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals. This repository does not currently have an NPR to AUD exchange rate, so an AUD estimate is not available. Permit and protected-area entry fees can be separate; check the current amount before payment.
